Posted October 28, 2002
Analysis By Richard Cowan

Today NORML issued a special press release (below) telling the media that the 2001 FBI 's annual Uniform Crime Report showed that marijuana arrests totalled 723,627 last year.

That is the second highest number ever, being just slightly lower than the record 734,498 arrests in 2000. It will be very interesting to see if any of the media actually report the numbers. NORML began trying to get the media to tell the people about the arrest data in the early 1990s. We even put the data on the letterhead for several years, but it was almost never reported.

To put the numbers into context, NORML observes that the total number of marijuana arrests far exceeds the total number of arrests for all violent crimes combined, including murder, manslaughter, forcible rape, robbery and aggravated assault.

There were more than 2.3 million arrests for crimes tracked by the FBI in 2001, down less than 1 percent from 2000. Murder, rape and every other violent crime except aggravated assault rose.

The 15,980 murders represented a 2.5% increase over 2000. There were 6,750 white murder victims. 6,446 victims were black.

The total value of stolen property was estimated to be $17.1 billion, and only about one third of stolen property was recovered. Police were able to make arrests in only about 20 percent of all crimes. Just 13% of burglaries resulted in arrests. Clearly the police resources used going after cannabis crimes could be better used protecting our lives and property, if that is really what the police are for.

Also in the news today was a Time/CNN poll showing that 72 percent of Americans oppose jailing marijuana users, which is to say that they favor what is commonly called decriminalization. That is precisely the reform being proposed for Canada, and which is drawing such strong opposition from DEAland.
See
Walters Concedes That Canada Can Legalize Cannabis If It Wants To, Which Was The Only True Thing He Said While In Montreal.

This same poll also showed that some 34% of Americans favor the full legalization of cannabis, which is up from 31% just two years ago. (Actually, that is probably within the margin of error in the poll, but it seems to accurately reflect the trend because the number favoring continued prohibition is below 60%, whereas in 2000 almost 67% said they favored continued prohibition.)

Only 19% actually favor jailing users.
See
We Are Winning! Almost One Third In DEAland Now Support " Legalization " of Marijuana 40% In The West. In the Face of the Massive Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign and Spin Control in Polling.

When the Reagan/Bush crack war to replace cannabis with crack was raging in 1986, some 78% opposed legalization, and only 18% supported it.

The new poll showed that support for medical cannabis now stands at 80%. That is also higher than ever.
See
Gallup Poll Shows 73% Favor Medical Marijuana;
29% Favor Outright " Legalization "!
So What Are The Politicians Really Afraid Of?

In the meantime, the Drug Czar's new prohibitionist propaganda campaign focuses almost entirely on cannabis and the new party line denies that there is any possible medical use of cannabis.

John Walters likes to say that medicine is not determined by voting. Of course, neither is the presidency, but he is still missing the point. The people are not voting on medical science when they support medical cannabis. They simply oppose arresting patients and their doctors and cannabis providers. They are voting on the use of police resources and the rights of privacy.

It is certainly possible for a majority to be wrong. Obviously, I disagree with the majority that opposes full legalization. However, it is useful to note that John Stuart Mill shared the Founding Fathers concern about majoritarianism. He said, There is no worse tyranny than that of a majority. The test of democracy is not that the majority should always get its way but how far minorities are respected. "

In other words, the majority was considered to be a danger to minority rights.

Certainly, that is well-illustrated in the opposition to legalization. However, what are we to make of a situation in which the majority favors the rights of the minority to use medical cannabis, and opposes jailing cannabis users, but the government blocks both the majority's views and the minority's rights? That is precisely the case today.
See
Live Free or Die In Pain. The Ignorance and Arrogance of the Quacks Who Deny Pain Relief to the Sick and Dying.

To understand the depth of the prohibitionist opposition to democracy, consider this press release from the Hassela Nordic Network (www.hnnsweden.com):

Press release October 24, 2002

USA: Drug czar John Walters has sounded the alarm on America's increasingly lax approach to the dangers of marijuana use by visiting the states of Arizona, Nevada and now Chicago to dispel apparent myths that are leading the public to soften their stance against the drug.

Walters countered the moves to relax drug laws saying, There is a kind of reefer madness-madness going on here.

The states of Arizona and Nevada are considering ballot initiatives to decriminalise marijuana use and other states have already passed laws allowing the medicinal use of marijuana.

Walters said, I made the decision to go into the states I went into reluctantly. I certainly understand the dangers of federal officials, a White House official, coming to a state and talking about a state ballot issue. We didn't use to do this. But I was contacted repeatedly by people in these states who are working in prevention who said they are being drowned out by misrepresentations by people who have a lot of money and who have millions of dollars to spend on these campaigns.

Walters highlighted the fact that the potency of marijuana has increased dramatically in recent years and demonstrated correlations between young people cutting classes, stealing, attacking others and destroying property with how often they smoke marijuana.

Walters firmly states that marijuana has no medicinal value and that science is not based on plebiscite. Science is based on fact.

HNN comment: Democracy is a noble governing philosophy although its downfall can be caused when the majority of people are misrepresented or misinformed. At such times it is necessary to protect democracy and gain a true understanding of what are the best policies for a nation or state by understanding the truth about the facts that influence that decision. We commend John Walters in his steps to not let pro-marijuana advocates mislead the public and destroy democracy through their financial weight. It is both within Walters's capacity and responsibility to take such steps in coordinating the war on drugs.

October 28, 2002

Marijuana Arrests For Year 2001 Second Highest Ever Despite Feds' War On
Terror, FBI Report Reveals

Washington, DC: Police arrested an estimated 723,627 persons for marijuana violations in 2001, according to the Federal Bureau of Investigation's annual Uniform Crime Report, released today. The total is the second highest ever recorded by the FBI, and comprises nearly half of all drug arrests in the United States.

" These numbers belie the myth that police do not target and arrest minor marijuana offenders, " said Keith Stroup, Executive Director of the National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws (NORML). " In fact, the war on drugs is largely a war on pot smokers. This effort is a tremendous waste of criminal justice resources that should be dedicated toward combating serious and violent crime, including the war on terrorism. "

Of those charged with marijuana violations, 88.6 percent - some 641,108 Americans - were charged with possession only. The remaining 82,518 individuals were charged with " sale/manufacture, " a category that includes all cultivation offenses even those where the marijuana was being grown for personal or medical use.

The total number of marijuana arrests far exceeds the total number of arrests for all violent crimes combined, including murder, manslaughter, forcible rape, robbery and aggravated assault.

Since 1992, approximately six million Americans have been arrested on marijuana charges, a greater number than the entire populations of Alaska, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Vermont and Wyoming combined. Annual marijuana arrests have nearly doubled in that time.

" It's time we stopped arresting adults who smoke marijuana responsibly, " says Stroup.

YEAR MARIJUANA ARRESTS
2001 723,627
2000 734,498
1999 704,812
1998 682,885
1997 695,200
1996 641,642
1995 588,963
1994 499,122
1993 380,689
1992 342,314
